questions.questionText: What is "Vishing"?

options.text: Video Phishing via webcam feeds.
Voice Phishing conducted via telephone calls or VoIP systems.
Virtual Firewall scanning.
Vector Analysis of server logs.

questions.explanation: Vishing is social engineering delivered via voice/phone communication.

questions.questionText: Caller ID information displayed on a smartphone screen can be easily spoofed by attackers using web VoIP services.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Caller ID metadata can be modified by outbound VoIP gateways to show fake names and numbers.

questions.questionText: You receive a call from "Corporate IT Support" stating your laptop is infected. The caller instructs you to go to a website and install AnyDesk so they can clean the machine. What should you do?

options.text: Install AnyDesk immediately to fix the laptop.
Decline the request, hang up, and verify the incident through official internal IT channels.
Give the caller your banking credentials instead.
Leave your laptop running and walk away.

questions.explanation: Installing remote desktop software on unsolicited calls gives attackers full control over your endpoint.

questions.questionText: Why is voice interaction (vishing) particularly effective at tricking targets compared to email?

options.text: Phone calls cannot be recorded.
Real-time vocal conversations create high cognitive pressure and leave little time for independent verification.
Emails are always blocked by antivirus software.
Voice calls automatically bypass password controls.

questions.explanation: Live dialogue creates urgency and emotional pressure, making critical analysis difficult.

questions.questionText: Which of the following information should you NEVER read aloud or share during an inbound phone call? *(Select TWO)*

options.text: Your work email address.
Your account password or PIN.
A Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) One-Time Password.
Your company's public website domain.

questions.explanation: Passwords and OTPs must remain confidential and should never be disclosed over inbound calls.

questions.questionText: Official company helpdesks frequently call remote workers unannounced to demand their personal email passwords.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Legitimate helpdesks do not require your private account passwords to perform administrative tasks.

questions.questionText: An incoming call displays your bank's exact toll-free phone number. The caller states: *"Security Alert: A $900 transfer was attempted. Read the code we just sent your phone to cancel it."* What should you do?

options.text: Read the code to the caller.
Hang up immediately, find the official phone number on your physical payment card, and call the bank directly.
Press 9 to transfer to police.
Give the caller your Social Security Number.

questions.explanation: Spoofed Caller ID makes fake calls appear genuine; hanging up and calling back independently confirms authenticity.

questions.questionText: What term describes repeated, automated MFA push prompts sent to a user’s phone to force them into tapping "Approve" out of frustration?

options.text: Denial of Service
MFA Fatigue / Push Bombing
Port Scanning
SQL Injection

questions.explanation: Push bombing bombards targets with MFA prompts until they accidentally or reactively accept one.

questions.questionText: Interactive Voice Response (IVR) robocall systems are only used by legitimate companies and cannot be set up by cybercriminals.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Attackers frequently create automated IVR phone trees to imitate official bank menus before transferring victims to live scammers.

questions.questionText: What is the primary objective of a vishing attacker who convinces a remote employee to install Quick Assist or TeamViewer?

options.text: To upgrade the computer's monitor resolution.
To establish an active remote control session to exfiltrate files and pivot into corporate networks.
To improve local Wi-Fi speeds.
To automatically clear browser cache.

questions.explanation: Remote administration tools grant full desktop GUI control to the adversary.

questions.questionText: A caller claims to be from the internal finance team: *"I am processing your remote equipment reimbursement, but the system is throwing an error. What is your full bank account and routing number?"* How should you respond?

options.text: Provide the numbers verbally.
Decline to share bank details over the phone and direct the inquiry to the official HR/Finance portal.
Give your credit card CVV number instead.
Hang up and delete your operating system.

questions.explanation: Financial distribution updates must follow encrypted, formal portal workflows rather than verbal disclosures.

questions.questionText: What is the best immediate response when an unknown caller becomes aggressive and demands immediate compliance?

options.text: Comply with their demands to avoid trouble.
Terminate the call (hang up) and report the incident to security.
Apologize and offer your personal credentials.
Hold the line for 5 hours without speaking.

questions.explanation: Aggressive emotional pressure is a hallmark of vishing; hanging up terminates the attack vector.

questions.questionText: Vishing attacks only target personal landline phones and cannot be conducted over corporate VoIP applications like Microsoft Teams or Zoom.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Attackers can initiate vishing via corporate VoIP, direct web calls, or messaging applications.

questions.questionText: Which technique helps mitigate the risk of Caller ID spoofing when receiving unexpected internal calls?

options.text: Trusting the Caller ID name unconditionally.
Independent Out-of-Band Callbacks using verified internal directory numbers.
Turning off smartphone Bluetooth.
Disabling mobile flight mode.

questions.explanation: Calling back via a independently verified number bypasses spoofed inbound routing.

questions.questionText: You receive an unexpected call: *"This is Executive Assistant Claire calling on behalf of CEO Mark. He needs you to purchase five digital gift cards right now for a client meeting."* What red flag is present?

options.text: Requests for digital gift cards combined with executive authority impersonation and urgency.
The caller used proper grammar.
The call occurred during business hours.
The caller knew the CEO's name.

questions.explanation: Requesting gift cards under executive pressure is a classic social engineering financial scam.

questions.questionText: Generative AI tools now allow vishing attackers to clone an executive's voice using short audio samples taken from public videos or webinars.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: AI voice cloning enables realistic synthetic audio impersonation of targeted individuals.

questions.questionText: What should a remote worker do if they accidentally approve a fraudulent MFA push prompt during a vishing call?

options.text: Keep quiet and hope no one notices.
Immediately report the incident to security, trigger an account password reset, and revoke active sessions.
Turn off the computer and throw it away.
Send a text to the scammer asking them to log out.

questions.explanation: Swift incident reporting enables security teams to isolate compromised sessions before lateral movement occurs.

questions.questionText: Which department should a remote employee contact to report a suspicious vishing call impersonating internal staff?

options.text: Local Sanitation Department
Enterprise Security / IT Security Incident Response Team
Public Library
The caller's personal number

questions.explanation: Security teams handle threat logging, account isolation, and incident analysis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following indicators suggest an incoming phone call is a vishing attempt? *(Select TWO)*

options.text: The caller demands that you bypass standard verification procedures due to an "emergency."
The caller asks you to read back an incoming SMS passcode.
The call was scheduled 3 days in advance via official calendar invite.
The caller tells you to check official corporate documentation without asking for data.

questions.explanation: Emergency protocol bypasses and requests for passcodes are primary vishing tactics.

questions.questionText: An official bank representative will hang up on you if you state that you are hanging up to call back via the number on your payment card.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Legitimate representatives encourage safe verification habits and welcome callbacks to official lines. MODULE 5: Pretexting
